model_output.verdict: A logistics and maintenance leader with a strong record of supervising people, equipment, and vehicle readiness.
write_up: Your resume makes a strong case for an operations supervisor role! Your Army progression from mechanic to Platoon Sergeant shows both hands-on maintenance work and leadership across maintenance, supply, and fuel.

The vehicle readiness line is the model: it shows a substantial improvement and names the changes you made to parts ordering and scheduling. The rest of the resume backs up your leadership with team counts, equipment accountability, and a parts budget.

Your resume is unlikely to be what holds you back. For civilian applications, consider explaining military terms in familiar operations language, and keep the readiness result prominent. How closely a job matches your experience and how competitive it is will matter too.

cards.line: - Cut the unit's vehicle non-mission-capable rate from 18% to 6% in a year by changing the parts ordering process and the weekly maintenance schedule
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model. The before-and-after figures give a recruiter something concrete to remember, and you take ownership of the work behind them.

fit.why: You're seeking an operations supervisor role, and your latest job combines team leadership with maintenance, supply, and fuel work.
fit.level: manager, led 38 soldiers and evaluated 6 direct-report sergeants
fit.note: Your maintenance leadership and inventory accountability also point toward roles overseeing equipment and supply operations. Your in-progress supply chain degree adds to that direction.
